indigo-light.note: System voice: answer ink, status/error, primary action, selected tool, indigo rules.

sheet-light.note: Writing surface; fills the whole page.

sheet-edge-light.note: Recessed tonal layer for slips, control capsule, calibration pad.

graphite-light.note: The hand's ink and primary text; default tool tint.

graphite-soft-light.note: Secondary labels, status line, faint body rules.

status.purpose: Single top-bar status line; graphite-soft normally, indigo on error.

confirmation-title.purpose: Recognized question read back in quotes.

recovery-headline.purpose: Error message on the recovery slip, tinted indigo.

control-label.purpose: Button labels, picker label, calibration prompts/captions.

answer-ink.purpose: The answer, drawn as real vector PKStroke ink in indigo — NOT type.

shadows.name: none
shadows.purpose: No drop shadows. Depth is tonal layering of native materials plus 1pt hairline rules only (The Flat-Paper Rule).

materials.name: sheet
materials.purpose: Full-bleed cool mineral paper; ignores safe areas.

materials.name: sheet-edge
materials.purpose: Recessed tonal fill for slips, tool capsule, calibration pad — conveys depth without shadow.

materials.name: body-rule
materials.purpose: Horizontal paper rules behind all ink; non-interactive, accessibility-hidden.

motion.name: slip-enter
motion.purpose: Confirmation/recovery slips rise from where the writing is.

motion.name: answer-reveal-stroke
motion.purpose: Per-stroke progressive reveal of answer ink in true drawing order; long answers scale points-per-frame up to stay within the bounded 15s target without changing stroke order.

motion.name: answer-reveal-reduced-line
motion.purpose: Reduce Motion: reveal whole lines instead of per-stroke motion.

motion.name: answer-reveal-reduced-immediate
motion.purpose: Reduce Motion (immediate mode) / recompose after style change once a reveal already completed.

adaptation.name: action-row
adaptation.trigger: labels too wide for width or large Dynamic Type
adaptation.invariant: 44pt hit targets preserved in both layouts
adaptation.note: There are no pixel breakpoints; adaptation is content/Dynamic-Type driven.

adaptation.name: scroll-sync
adaptation.strategy: single scrollable question canvas publishes contentOffset; answer canvas mirrors it
adaptation.invariant: answer pinned in the question's absolute page coordinate space below the question; ~240pt trailing margin reserved

presetHands.name: Slanted
presetHands.character: Fast rightward slant, tighter tracking, more variation.

presetHands.name: Personal
presetHands.note: Locally calibrated hand; stroke geometry stays on-device.

narrative.overview:
Living Page is one quiet sheet of cool mineral paper you write a question onto by hand and watch answer itself. It refuses the chat category default outright: there is no message list, no card grid, no typing field, no send box. The page IS both the input and the output. Graphite ink carries everything the hand makes; deep indigo is reserved for the system's voice — the status line and the answer, which is written as real vector ink in the same synchronized page plane as the question rather than set as UI text. Native SF typography and SF Symbols do the plumbing so the interface itself stays silent and the ink is the only thing that speaks.

The system is restrained to the point of near-invisibility at rest. On launch the whole sheet is the surface: a faint ruled body with a left-margin rule, a single quiet status line ("Write a question."), the style picker, and the bottom-trailing pen/eraser/clear controls. Nothing else competes; there is no onboarding card, no modal, no keyboard. Controls are quiet, standard, HIG-native, and physically large enough for a hand holding a Pencil. The magic is meant to come entirely from authentic ink behavior — real strokes revealing themselves in indigo below the question — not from ornament, glow, or novelty effects.

Depth is expressed by tonal layering of native materials rather than by shadow craft: the sheet, a slightly recessed sheet edge, and quiet indigo/graphite rules stack to read as one continuous piece of paper. Both light and dark are first-class; every color is authored as a light/dark pair so the folio reads as the same sheet under either appearance.
keyCharacteristics: One sheet: the page is simultaneously the question input and the answer output.
Graphite for the hand, deep indigo for the system's single voice.
The answer is real vector ink (PKStroke), never a font or Text.
Quiet native/HIG controls with 44pt hit targets; nothing competes with the ink.
Light and dark authored as equal pairs; flat tonal paper, no parchment, no franchise imagery.

rules.name: The One-Voice Indigo Rule
rules.body: Deep indigo belongs to the system alone. It appears only where the app is speaking — the answer ink, the status/error line, the primary confirm/retry action, calibration progress and rules. The hand never writes in indigo; graphite is the human, indigo is the page answering back. Its rarity is what makes the answer feel alive.

rules.name: The Ink-Not-Type Rule
rules.body: The answer is never a font, Text, raster image, or glyph outline. It is the exact PKDrawing produced by the ink compositor, revealed as real vector strokes in the same synchronized page plane as the question. System type is allowed only for controls, status, and labels — never for the answer itself.

rules.name: The Flat-Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Never add drop shadows, glows, or bevels to lift an element. Separation comes from the sheet-edge tonal fill and hairline rules, so the whole app continues to read as one continuous sheet under both light and dark.

dos: Do keep deep indigo for the system's voice only — answer ink, status/error, the primary confirm/retry action (the One-Voice Indigo Rule).
Do render every answer and personalized preview as real vector PKStroke ink, never as a font or Text (the Ink-Not-Type Rule).
Do hold surfaces flat and build depth from the sheet-edge tonal fill and hairline rules only (the Flat-Paper Rule).
Do preserve 44pt hit targets and use ViewThatFits (horizontal row → vertical stack) so slips and calibration controls adapt to width and large Dynamic Type.
Do use 24pt outer insets, 18pt slip corners, and the 44pt body-rule rhythm as the durable spatial constants.
Do author every color as a light/dark pair so the folio is equally first-class in dark mode.
Do honor Reduce Motion by swapping the per-stroke reveal for line-level or immediate reveal and replacing slip move transitions with a plain opacity fade.
Do keep the answer pinned in the question's absolute coordinate space by mirroring the single scrollable surface's offset.
donts: Don't introduce a message list, card grid, typing field, send box, or any chat-bubble metaphor — the single sheet is both input and output.
Don't add parchment textures, glows, ornament, or any Harry Potter / franchise imagery, fonts, crests, or sounds (the no-franchise / no-parchment guardrail).
Don't let the hand write in indigo or let the system speak in graphite; the two voices never swap.
Don't set the answer as a handwriting font, styled Text, or raster image.
Don't add drop shadows, bevels, or lift effects to separate surfaces.
Don't promote a single surface's composition into a global rule; only the durable single-sheet principles above are system-wide.
